eval.title: NIO Stock Full Analysis | Bull (Tesla of China) & Bear (China) Thesis

call.headline_quote: buying neo now is a very risky or we can say stupid think because of all the risks

base_metric.name: fcf_per_share
base_metric.quote: 2.5 billion in cash flow divided by 2.5 it's one dollar in free cash flow per share

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: if they grow then at 15 next and have a 50 multiple in 2030 so a car company in 2030 with slower growth from 2030 onward having a 50 multiple then i'm justifying the current stock price

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: let's say have double the margins and 20 growth from 2025 on free cash flows terminal multiple 40 then you justify a higher stock price double the current stock price

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: my worst case scenario would be that it never makes any money

what_is_priced_in.quote: 1.2 million cars a little bit more 15 growth discount rate 5 terminal multiple 30 in 2030 and we get to an intrinsic value of 95 billion

reasons.claim: At the current price you already need a 5% return assumption to justify it, and only the most exuberant scenario gets you to a 10% return; that is not attractive risk/reward.
reasons.quote: if you are hoping for a 5 return from your neo investment if you're hoping for a 10 return then neo is almost 100 undervalued in the most exuberant cases let's say fairly valued

data_check.gap_note: he says 1, as-of -1.49796e+09 (FY2019); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: NIO has burned enormous cash per car sold and will need to massively dilute shareholders to fund the ramp from 40,000 to 600,000+ cars, likely doubling share count.
reasons.quote: in the last four or five years they have burned 7.5 billion dollars 7.5 billion dollars to sell 700 to sell 70 000 cars

data_check.gap_note: he says 7.5e+09, as-of 1.23939e+08 (FY2019); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: cars sold

reasons.claim: The Chinese government bailout restructured ownership so US shareholders only own a shell holding a stake in NIO-China, which controls all the real assets and can dilute owners further on Beijing's terms, not Wall Street's.
reasons.quote: you're not owning the complete company the chinese government is owning neo china and you're just owning a shell owning a percentage of neo-china

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: NEO stake in NEO-China

reasons.claim: Intense and rising competition from Tesla, XPeng, and even Apple shows there is no real moat, and if Tesla is forced to cut prices, smaller players like NIO cannot make money either.
reasons.quote: even tesla had to slash its car price by eight percent to sell the inventory so that's insane that just shows you how there is no moat in the market

data_check.gap_note: he says 8, as-of 57 (2021-01-29); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Wall Street analysts are extremely bullish because their banks are underwriting NIO's convertible bond and share issuances, so their bullishness is conflicted and not to be trusted.
reasons.quote: so of course they are going to be extremely bullish on all these hot stocks because as we discuss in the jeremy grantham video that's the incentive for wall street you make your money in wall street by having the bubble keep going
